name: Earth science: Atlantic hurricane track forecasting from the best track
description: Fit a statistical tropical-cyclone track model on the 1950-2014 Atlantic best track and forecast 12-120 h centre positions for every advisory-time record of the held-out 2015-2024 storms. The score is the mean great-circle track error over seven lead times.

sources.locator: Aberson (1998): CLIPER5, the climatology-and-persistence five-day Atlantic track forecast used as the no-skill baseline.
Landsea and Franklin (2013): HURDAT2 format, content and best-track uncertainty.
HURDAT2 Atlantic best track, release of 4 April 2025 (1851-2024); public domain; the 1950-2024 synoptic records are used.
NHC 2024 forecast verification report: Tables 2 and 4 give 2019-2023 mean official, CLIPER5 and Decay-SHIFOR5 errors by lead.

requirements.datasets: Derived from pinned public sources by python3 scripts/prepare_earth.py (hashes in catalog/earth-data-lock.json).

evaluation.benchmark: Earth science: Atlantic hurricane track forecasting from the best track
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: fit_track_model(training_storms) -> model; model.forecast(history) -> float array (7, 2) of [latitude deg N, longitude deg E] forecast centre positions at 12, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96 and 120 h. Storms are dicts with numpy arrays time_hours (hours since 1950-01-01 00 UTC), month, day, hour, day_of_year, lat (deg N), lon (deg E, west negative), vmax_kt, mslp_hpa (NaN when missing), plus year (int) and status (list of HURDAT2 codes TD, TS, HU, EX, SD, SS, LO, WV, DB), one entry per 6-hourly synoptic record. training_storms are the 1950-2014 Atlantic HURDAT2 storms. Forecasts are requested in chronological order for every 6-hourly record of a held-out 2015-2024 storm at which it is TD/TS/HU/SD/SS and that verifies at one or more leads; history holds that storm's records up to and including the forecast time and nothing later. A lead verifies only if the storm is still TD/TS/HU/SD/SS at the verifying time (NHC convention). The candidate runs in a separate sandboxed process (numpy, scipy, scikit-learn and pandas importable; no file, network or subprocess access; one thread) with 120 s of CPU time for fitting and all predictions together; seed any randomness so that results are deterministic. Score: mean over the seven leads of the mean great-circle distance (km, sphere radius 6371 km) between forecast and best-track positions; lower is better. Latitudes outside [-90, 90], longitudes outside [-360, 360], NaN or wrong shapes are invalid

limitations: Only best-track history is available to the candidate (position, intensity, pressure, stage and date); operational forecasts also use satellite and reconnaissance analyses and numerical weather prediction, so scores are not comparable with official NHC errors.
Inputs are the post-season best track rather than the real-time operational estimates; verification is at 6-hourly synoptic times only, and off-synoptic landfall records are dropped.
A better score is a better statistical track model on these seasons, not a scientific discovery.
The held-out observations are public, so search feedback on this fixed split can overfit it; freeze a candidate and test it on later or independent data before claiming a scientific improvement.

The candidate runs in a sandboxed child process that receives a storm's best track only up to the forecast time, and no statement of the candidate is executed in the evaluator's process; outside macOS (kernel sandbox) deliberately hostile native code could bypass the file policy.

state_of_the_art.statement: No published value exists for this exact protocol. For context, NHC reports 2019-2023 mean Atlantic official track errors of 23.9, 36.5, 49.3, 63.4, 93.4, 132.9 and 190.4 n mi at 12, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96 and 120 h (forecasts built with full numerical guidance) and CLIPER5 errors of 45.7, 97.1, 153.0, 205.4, 297.8, 372.7 and 439.1 n mi on a different (operational, homogeneous) sample.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Predict where an Atlantic tropical cyclone's centre will be one to five days ahead.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Track forecasts drive hurricane watches, warnings and evacuations; climatology-and-persistence models are the reference against which forecast skill is measured.

papers.title: Five-Day Tropical Cyclone Track Forecasts in the North Atlantic Basin
papers.primary_goal: Develop and evaluate a statistical climatology-and-persistence model (CLIPER5) that forecasts Atlantic tropical cyclone tracks out to five days.
papers.task_relation: The task asks for the same kind of history-only statistical track forecast, verified against the best track at 12-120 h; it uses the 2015-2024 seasons and a simplified verification rather than the paper's sample.

science_relevance.reason: The cited paper's main goal is forecasting tropical cyclone tracks from climatology and persistence, which is what the local task scores; no reproduction of its numbers is claimed.
science_relevance.verification_basis: Crossref metadata and the NHC 2024 verification report (CLIPER5 description and error tables) inspected; local evaluator run on the pinned HURDAT2 release.
science_relevance.definition: A task is important to science when it addresses a substantive scientific or real-world problem, and a cited research paper's main objective is to solve that problem or advance understanding of it. The evidence must explain why the problem matters and how the local task represents it.
